data: Politics in Multiple Frames: Approaches, concepts and theoretical perspectives

This course seeks to outline various perspectives of understanding politics at multiple levels from the local to the national to the global. Is politics essentially about power, government and elections, or is it about friends and foes? Could it be about a deep yet contested conversation about public goods or an art of bringing political differences into an integral but tension-ridden whole? Students will develop a foundational understanding of historical, empirical and normative dimensions of politics at each of these scales. What are the pressing questions that we encounter at different levels of politics, and how did the systems that organise them come to be, and what are the epistemologies and power dynamics that underpin them? How does the academic discipline of politics constitute its objects of study and protocols of enquiry? Can the focus of politics be exclusively on human action, and such a focus be sustained in times of deep ecological crises?
